title: Throughput Spectrometer and Customer Gauge
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a repeatable benchmarking and customer acceptance artifact called the 'Throughput Spectrometer' that converts customer traces into a calibrated synthetic workload, runs spectrally-aware load experiments against Dedicated pools, and produces a sign-off 'Customer Gauge' report for sales/solutions/CE teams. This ticket owns the measurement methodology, test harness integration, autoscaling stability scenarios, and the acceptance checklist used for customer on-boarding of Dedicated capacity commitments.
acceptance_criteria: Spectral conversion tool (trace2spectrum) implemented and validated on 3 customer traces: chat-sparse, chat-dense, embedding-burst
Benchmark harness runs reproducible experiments with <5% variance on p95 latency across 5 repeated runs for steady-state loads
Autoscaler-policy experiments show no SLA violations during scale-up windows for configured policies (step, predictive, hysteresis) across 10 minute ramps
Customer Gauge report template auto-populates with workload fingerprint, expected QPS, recommended autoscaling profile, quantization suggestion, and a binary sign-off indicator
End-to-end run documented with runbook links and a sample GitHub artifact that contains raw measurements and plots
test_plan: Phase 1: Instrumentation and spectral analysis - implement trace2spectrum to extract inter-arrival distribution, token-length histogram, prefix-correlation matrix
Phase 2: Synthetic workload generator - emit requests preserving spectral properties and KV-cache locality; support variable token-stream and response sizes
Phase 3: Harness integration - add orchestration for stepped ramps (ramp, sustain, microbursts, decay) and steady-state sweeps; integrate with telemetry exporter
Phase 4: Autoscaling scenarios - run canonical policies: step-scale (X->Y), predictive scale (based on short-term trend), and hysteresis-enabled scale-down; validate safety windows
Phase 5: Fleet-control safety - inject node failure and capacity loss events during sustained loads to validate graceful fallback rules and model-variant routing
Phase 6: Customer acceptance run - convert one anonymized customer trace, run the Spectrometer, generate Customer Gauge, and walk through sign-off checklist with Solutions Engineering
measurement_methods: Use token-level latency histograms and request-level traces correlated to GPU kernel metrics
Report p50/p90/p95/p99 and tail quantiles with confidence intervals computed from repeated runs
Measure cost per 1K tokens using accounting hooks during each experiment run
Capture autoscaler events with timestamps to map latency spikes to scale actions
notes: We intentionally focus on spectral fidelity (inter-arrival/token-size correlation) rather than naive QPS replay to better preserve KV cache behavior.
Calibration routine includes a short 'fingerprint run' to estimate effective batching and pad down/up the synthetic generator to match observed latency distributions.
We will aim to keep a canonical set of 3 workload fingerprints for sales demos: conversational-low, conversational-high, and embedding-spike.
Quantization and model-variant recommendations are advisory; separate validation ticket required for functional-quality regression checks.
